_comment: Delta Rentals Dubai (TRIPLE D RENTALS L.L.C.). Figures imported from their published terms at deltarentalsdubai.com/terms. THIS REMAINS A DEMONSTRATION CONFIGURATION until every entry in _assumed is confirmed by the operator. Real figures under a real company name make a wrong answer more damaging, not less.

rental_period._past_pickup_comment: A rental cannot start before now. The tolerance covers a customer saying 'right now' while the clock ticks past, and ordinary clock skew — it is not a licence to book last week.
rental_period._window_comment: Sanity bounds on the window itself. A booking from 7:00pm to 7:01pm, or one starting in the year 3000, is a data-entry error rather than a rental — and quoting a price for either makes the company look like it is not paying attention.

required_documents.notes: Documents are simulated in the prototype. No real identity data is verified or stored.

deposit.source: Listings state no deposit required (T&Cs apply).
deposit.notes: Numbered agreement 3.1 gives a range of AED 5,000-20,000 subject to vehicle, driver and duration, so no single figure can be quoted. 3.2 holds it for 30 days. A paid, non-refundable no-deposit option exists (4.1) whose fee is published nowhere.

mileage.source: 250 km per day, per the vehicle listings.

delivery.notes: Free delivery and collection within Dubai between 09:00 and 22:00 (numbered agreement 6.1); outside those hours a fee applies (6.2). Delivery outside Dubai or beyond 30 km of the business location is charged by agreement and is NOT a published figure — see _pending_confirmation.

airport._comment: Timing a delivery to meet a flight. The buffer is how long after the aircraft is on the ground before the customer is at the kerb — immigration, baggage, the walk. Their own team quoted about an hour in the conversations we have. Confirm it: questionnaire 17 covers delivery beyond the usual, and this is the same kind of question.

discount_policy.notes: A customer's claim about a past discount is never evidence. Only this policy grants discounts.
discount_policy._comment: Delta publishes NO discount policy. Every ceiling is therefore zero: with no authority on file the agent must not invent one, and a discount request escalates to a person who can actually decide. Replace these with the operator's real ladder before go-live — until then, zero is the only honest value, because a percentage offered on a real company's real price is money out of their pocket that nobody authorised.

extension.notes: Written approval and pre-payment required. Unauthorised extensions are charged at double the daily rate.

insurance.included: Basic comprehensive, per the vehicle listings.
insurance._cdw_excess_comment: Numbered agreement 17.2: an excess 'starting from AED 5,000 up to depending on the car model and determined by the insurance provider'. So this is a floor, not the figure. The agent must say 'from', never state it as the amount owed — understating what someone could owe after an accident is the mistake that matters here.

payment.notes: All payments in this prototype are SIMULATED.

links._comment: Their brief section 2 asks for a link generated from the quoted price. Their terms say 'you will only pay when you pick up your car', and across thirteen conversations nobody ever sent one — what they take in advance is a holding payment to secure a specific car. So what the link charges is a question for them (questionnaire 22), and until they answer it the safe default is the rental total, which the engine always knows.
links._holding_amount_note: Their team quotes AED 500 to secure a booking, and once USD 300. Left null until confirmed — a holding payment is money taken from a real customer.

human_in_the_loop._comment: What happens after the agent hands a case to a person. The agent's job at this point is to stop guessing, ask a decidable question, and relay the answer accurately — never to soften it or fill the gap while waiting.
human_in_the_loop._kinds_comment: Three kinds, not two. A fee dispute is a DECISION: two answers exist and the owner picks one. A crash is a HANDOVER: nothing to pick, a person takes over. A deposit the operator has never published is an ANSWER: the owner knows the figure and nobody else does, so the reply is a value rather than a choice. Putting Approve/Decline in front of 'what is the deposit?' is the same mistake as putting them in front of a car accident.

owner_handover._comment: Everything not listed as a decision. The owner is told to take over rather than asked to choose, and one button releases the conversation once they have.

owner_decision._comment: Three buttons is the Cloud API maximum and titles are capped at 20 characters. Ids are matched in code, so renaming a label is safe but renaming an id is not.

customer_messages._comment: The only two messages sent without the model. Everything else the customer hears is written by the agent, including the resolution itself — these two exist for the moments when there is nothing to be clever about and no decision to relay yet.
customer_messages.already_waiting: I'm still waiting to hear back on that one — I'll message you the moment I know.
customer_messages.timed_out: Sorry to keep you waiting on this. I haven't been able to reach a colleague yet, so I'm chasing it now and will come back to you as soon as I have an answer.

reopen_template._comment: WhatsApp only delivers free-form messages for 24 hours after a customer writes. Past that, this pre-approved template is the only way to reach them. Its job is to earn a reply — once they answer, the window reopens and the agent delivers the real decision in its own words. The operator must have this approved in Meta Business Manager (category: UTILITY) before going live; the name here must match theirs exactly.
reopen_template.name: case_update
reopen_template.approved_body: Hi {{1}}, I have an update on the issue you raised with us. Reply to this message and I'll go through it with you.

overrides._comment: An owner may exceed the rules for one case — it is their business. What must never happen is that decision becoming policy: it is recorded against this reservation only, kept out of the learning loop, and the next customer is quoted the standard rules.

human_in_the_loop._unconfirmed_figure_comment: A customer asking for a figure the operator has not confirmed — the deposit, the no-deposit service fee, a per-km rate. The agent has no way to reach it, so without somewhere to send the question it invents a future in which the figure appears: 'the system calculates it at the final stage', 'we lock it in at the reservation stage'. There is no such stage. Ask a person once, and tell the customer that is what you did.

owner_answer._comment: The owner is asked for the figure itself. Their free text becomes the answer and is relayed verbatim, so it is treated as authorised evidence and the agent may state it. One button remains, for an owner who would rather deal with the customer directly.
owner_answer.ask: *Reply with the figure* and I'll pass it straight on. I won't guess at it.

owner_decision_by_reason._comment: Approve and Decline are right for a fee dispute and wrong for a held car — the owner is being asked whether it is actually free, and the words should say so.

booking_hold.ask: *Is this car actually free?* Confirm and I'll tell them it's booked. If it is out, I'll say so and find them something else.

messaging._comment: How the agent behaves as a WhatsApp participant rather than as a text generator. Pacing and reactions are configuration, not code, so an operator can retune the feel without a deploy.

pacing._comment: The first message goes out immediately; only follow-ups are paced. A customer should get an answer fast and then watch the detail arrive, which is what a person does.

reactions._comment: A reaction reports what the engine did, never what the model felt. Nulls are deliberate: an emoji on an accident report would be grotesque, so escalation is silent by rule rather than by omission.

demo_disclosure.required_footer: This is a demonstration booking. No real vehicle is reserved and no payment is taken.

_source: deltarentalsdubai.com/terms-conditions/, numbered Vehicle Rental Agreement sections 1-26. That page also carries an older, superseded agreement which disagrees on roughly twelve figures; the numbered one is treated as current.

_assumed._comment: Their terms give ranges where the engine needs one value. Confirm each.
_assumed.deposit: Listings say 'no deposit required'; the terms say AED 5,000-20,000 varying by vehicle, driver and duration, plus a non-refundable no-deposit option. Encoded as 0 to match the listings. Needs a per-category answer.
_assumed.insurance_excess: Terms say 'AED 5,000+ depending on vehicle', plus a minimum 20% hirer liability and 30-100% of car value by fault. Encoded flat at 5000. Needs a per-category answer.
_assumed.extra_km_price: AED 25-150/km by vehicle. Left at 0 on every car rather than guessed.
_assumed.mileage: 200-250 km/day by vehicle. All set to 250, which is what the listings show.
_assumed.discount_policy: Delta publishes no discount ladder at all. The ceilings here are INVENTED and must be replaced before go-live — this is the one block most likely to cost them money.
_assumed.smoking_penalty: AED 2,500-5,000. Not encoded as a computed fee.
_assumed.minimum_age_supercar: Terms say 23-25 for supercars. Set to 25, the conservative end.

_pending_confirmation._comment: Published as ranges or not published at all. The agent must not state any of these — it says the team confirms it for the specific vehicle. Each becomes a real value the moment the operator answers.
_pending_confirmation.deposit_by_category: 3.1: AED 5,000-20,000, subject to vehicle, driver profile and duration.
_pending_confirmation.no_deposit_option_fee: 4.1: exists and is non-refundable. Amount published nowhere.
_pending_confirmation.extra_km_price: 8.2: AED 25-150 per km depending on vehicle. Superseded doc says 25-50.
_pending_confirmation.insurance_excess: 17.2: from AED 5,000 upward, set by the insurer per vehicle.
_pending_confirmation.damage_liability_share: 17.3 and 17.6: minimum 20% of damage cost, and 30-100% of car value.
_pending_confirmation.delivery_outside_dubai: 6.5: charged by agreement depending on location.
_pending_confirmation.minimum_age_sports: 5.1: 23-25 for sports and supercars, vehicle dependent. Held at 25 because turning away an eligible customer costs less than refusing one at handover.
_pending_confirmation.weekly_monthly_rates: Listed publicly as 'on request'; the engine bills daily x days.

booking._comment: The booking provider decides whether a booking exists (BOOKING_PROVIDER). The simulated provider is authoritative for demo inventory and confirms outright; a provider that cannot settle availability leaves every booking a request a person confirms, whatever this flag says. Set holds_require_confirmation true to force a person into the loop even where the provider could confirm — which is what Delta needs the day a real connector exists but their phone and counter bookings still are not in it.
